- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially when sentiment is neutral or positive — model tends to push prices higher than true mean reversion.
- Underestimate sharp downward moves after recent spikes — model fails to recognize momentum reversal or policy-driven corrections.
- Overshoots in 30-day forecasts when recent price action shows strong downward trend — model retains inertia from prior peaks.
- When sentiment is negative (even if not explicitly recorded), model still overconfidently forecasts upward — adjust downward bias by 5–10% in such cases.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high for 10–15 days after peak, then underreacts to subsequent drops — apply smoothing filter to reduce lagged overestimation.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early days (1–7) and underestimate late days (24–30) — apply asymmetric decay weighting to forecast weights.
